Porsche Center Lock Recall Welcomes 548 Additional 911 and 718 Vehicles
33 photos
Photo: Porsche
Porsche is urging the owners of 548 vehicles to keep the cars parked until a dealer checks their wheels. Per the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the center locks can fracture, allowing the wheels to detach while driving. Filed under campaign 26V682, this recall expands on 24V809 from October 8, 2024.
The 548 additional vehicles were identified when Porsche matched supplier data against production dates and vehicle build records, a traceability exercise that revealed gaps the first investigation somehow missed. Anyway, the affected population comprises 2024 models exclusively.
Subject models range from the Carrera GTS to the GT3 RS and Cayman GT4 RS. The Carrera GTS leads with 168 potentially affected units in the US market, followed by the Turbo S at 94, the Cayman GT4 RS at 73, the Spyder RS at 70, the GT3 at 50, the GT3 RS at 41, the S/T at 39, and the Turbo at 13.
Before going any further, we should explain that center locks hold the wheels to the hub in lieu of the classic five-lug pattern. The centerlock system is a motorsport-inspired affair that saves weight and looks much cooler on performance-oriented vehicles. In motorsports, center locks speed up pit stops.
Regarding the center locks of the affected population, the clamping force is concentrated in a single component. When said component fractures, the wheel separates from the hub, increasing the risk of a crash. According to Porsche, owners may feel perceptible vibration before the wheel detaches from the hub.
Photo: Porsche Two field incidents in May 2026 and the month of August 2026, both involving fractured center locks, pushed the Zuffenhausen-based manufacturer back to the supplier. Thankfully for everyone, no injuries were reported.
The follow-up investigation with Hirschvogel, specifically the supplier of the central locking wheel component, found that previously unidentified material movements within the manufacturing and logistics processes had escaped the traceability assessment.
Hirschvogel and Porsche determined that additional suspect center locks came from the same material batch as the first recall, with both parties identifying specific delivery notes tied to that batch. Subject center locks were used on 2024 models produced between June 7, 2024, and July 19, 2024.
The fix is the same as before, with dealers required to inspect the fastening system. If anything seems wrong, potentially defective parts will be replaced at no charge to affected customers. The replacement center locks are said to come from a properly specified batch. Porsche will be reaching owners by email, push notification, and phone in the weeks following the 26V682 filing.
Formal customer letters should follow in the next couple of months. In any case, all customers will be notified by the end of December 2026. In the meantime, owners are urged not to drive their vehicles. The easiest way for customers to determine right now if their 911s and 718s need the remedy is to run the 17-character VIN on the automaker's website or the NHTSA's portal.

Troriluzole, in development for spinocerebellar ataxia, was rejected nearly a year ago when the FDA took issue with the design of Biohaven’s registrational study. The agency has now agreed to review a new application and render a decision in the first quarter of 2027.
Shares of Biohaven popped by as much as 36% on Thursday morning after the company disclosed the FDA’s acceptance of a resubmission for troriluzole—which the agency rejected late last year—in the rare, degenerative disorder spinocerebellar ataxia.
The FDA has assigned a new action date for troriluzole—also known as Vyglxia—in the first quarter of next year, according to a Thursday SEC filing . The agency also intends to hold an advisory committee meeting for the application, according to the document. A date for the adcomm will be set “in the near term.”
“The Vyglxia AdCom will be the most de-risking event here,” William Blair wrote to investors Thursday morning, citing the FDA’s previous reluctance to accept Biohaven’s three-year real-world evidence trial. Coined study 206-RWE, the program compared troriluzole to a natural history database on a movement scale modified for spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA) as primary evidence to support effectiveness.
SCA is a group of rare diseases that lead to the progressive loss of control over movement. Many types of the disease are genetic and there is currently no cure.
The FDA issued a complete response letter (CRL) for troriluzole’s use in SCA in November 2025, citing “issues that can be inherent to real-world evidence and external control studies including potential bias” and spurring a contentious reaction from Biohaven.
“We are extremely disappointed on behalf of patients by this action from the Office of Neuroscience at FDA,” CEO Vlad Coric said in a statement following the rejection. “Beyond substantial evidence of safety and efficacy, patients with rare diseases also deserve an efficient, fair and flexible regulatory process that aligns with the urgency of their high unmet medical needs.”
Prior to finalizing the Phase 3 study design, Biohaven had received feedback from the FDA warning that “a large and robust treatment effect would be needed to overcome the biases of an externally controlled trial, in order for it to be used as the primary basis for substantial evidence for effectiveness,” according to a Nov. 4, 2025, press release from Biohaven. But the biotech believed it had achieved this goal.

“Biohaven believes the statistical significance and clinical meaningfulness achieved on the primary endpoint and eight consecutive secondary endpoints in 206-RWE . . . clearly met criteria of ‘a large and robust treatment effect,’” the company said after receiving the CRL.
The regulatory rejection led Biohaven to cut R&D spending by 60% and caused its stock to crater by nearly 45% to $7.60 per share. As of 10:40 am ET on Thursday, shares of the biotech had risen to $15.41, 30% higher than yesterday’s closing price.
The resubmission includes new positive supportive analyses and the FDA said it considers the application a complete response to the Nov. 4 CRL, according to Biohaven’s SEC filing.
“Overall, we continue to see the risk/benefit of troriluzole as favorable in SCA, where there is no currently approved FDA therapy,” William Blair wrote on Thursday.
Despite missing the Phase 3 study’s primary endpoint of f-SARA—a modified scale designed specifically for SCA that focuses on sitting, standing, walking and talking—comparisons to natural history controls showed a 50–70% slower rate of decline for patients taking a 200 mg dose of Biohaven’s drug, William Blair noted, representing a delay of 1.5–2.2 years in disease progression over three years.

Dealer Sells a 1975 Pontiac Trans Am That Checks Almost All the Right Boxes, Numbers Matching
91 photos
Photo: Classic Auto Mall
A 1975 Pontiac Trans Am is looking for a new owner, and a dealer promises that you’ll get almost the perfect package, including matching numbers. A Trans Am that checks all the right boxes isn’t typically very hard to find, but the 1975 model year is significantly rarer.
The reason is simple. Many of these cars have already been altered - this is the case of this specimen, too, but bringing it back to a factory configuration shouldn’t be difficult - while others have ended up becoming rust buckets after years on the side of the road.
This Trans Am wears the correct paint and the screaming chicken that sets this Firebird version aside from the rest of the crowd. It’s unclear if this is the original paint, but no matter if it is, it already shows its age. It suffers from obvious bubbling, chips, and dings, so my recommendation is that you call the dealer and go see the car in person.
The dealer says there is “evidence of filler on rear fenders,” so yes, some bodywork has already been performed at some point in the past, so you’ll have to check everything thoroughly.
Photo: Classic Auto Mall The car wears an otherwise beautiful Buccaneer Red. The Trans Am color lineup was expanded to four choices in 1975, and Buccaneer Red was one of them. The rest of the choices were Sterling silver, Cameo White, and Stella Blue (whose mission was to replace Admiralty Blue).
The Trans Am was gaining ground gradually, and in 1975, it became the best-selling Firebird version in the entire line.
Pontiac sold over 84K Firebirds this year, and the Trans Am accounted for 27,274 units. The base Firebird was the runner-up with 22,293 cars, while the Esprit was third with 20,826 cars. The Formula was the last choice for Firebird buyers in 1975, getting only 13,670 orders.
The Trans Am was offered only with a 400 when the new model year was revealed, but buyers wanted more power, so Pontiac eventually reintroduced the 455 after only a few months. The 455 HO was exclusive with a 4-speed manual transmission and produced 200 horsepower.
However, the 400 continued to dominate the lineup, accounting for no more, no less than 26,417 orders. Most of these cars got an automatic transmission. Only 6,140 Trans Ams powered by an L78 were fitted with a manual.
Photo: Classic Auto Mall The same engine is also under the hood of this Trans Am, and according to the seller, this is the numbers-matching configuration. It is paired with a correct T10 4-speed manual transmission and comes alongside power brakes and power steering.
Everything is in running condition, so if you want to take the car for a short trip, you should be able to do this when you go there in person to inspect the Trans Am.
While the body shows its age, the undercarriage also requires some work. There’s surface rust and residual oil, but there’s nothing that a good metal guy wouldn’t be able to deal with. I’ve seen so many cars in worse shape getting fixed, so giving a second chance to this Trans Am shouldn’t require much effort.
The interior is the one that looks pretty cool, and the dealer says the “seat vinyl is completely intact all the way around.” Unfortunately, a previous owner decided to step away from the car’s day-one setup, so you’ll be getting an AM/FM/CD player.
Fortunately, a vintage 8-track player is also available, but please remove the CD player first because such a modern thing has no place in a classic car.
Photo: Classic Auto Mall Otherwise, this Trans Am is quite an intriguing car, especially if you’re not necessarily interested in working on it to return it to a day-one shape. This Trans Am can be driven as is, but depending on your expectations and budget, you can also spend a few more bucks to deal with all the issues I highlighted earlier.
My recommendation is that you still inspect the car live because I don’t think the photos do enough justice to this Trans Am. I wouldn’t be surprised to see the car looking even better in real person, especially because the paint doesn’t look all that bad. Buccaneer Red is a gorgeous finish anyway, especially when it’s not entirely gone.
The dealer is asking $31,900 for this Trans Am, but it also enabled the Make Offer option on eBay, so the door might be open for further negotiations. It’s up to you to make an offer the dealer can’t refuse, so click this button and reach out to the seller while you still can.
This is because the Trans Am will go offline in 4 days, unless someone clicks the Buy It Now button earlier. If you want to see this Trans Am with your own eyes, you must pack your bags and prepare for a trip to Morgantown, Pennsylvania.

Son's Barn-Found Oldsmobile Needs Restoration After Spending 47 Years in Storage
45 photos
Photo: eBay seller 383-runner
Here’s something you don’t see every day. This 1966 Oldsmobile spent no more, no less than 47 years locked in a barn, away from the road and away from humanity. The reason why it’s online is pretty simple: it’s now ready to go, so if you’re somehow interested in restoring a nice Olds, this Starfire is certainly worth checking out.
Bought by the seller’s son in March this year, this Oldsmobile is obviously a project whose only option is a complete restoration.
The closer you get, and the deeper you dig, the more problems you’ll find, but these shouldn’t necessarily be a reason to walk away for those who’ve come across classic cars before. An engine that no longer starts and metal corrosion are something very common in this space.
Photo: eBay seller 383-runner The Starfire could only be had as a coupe in 1966. It was the only model available in a single configuration, as every other Oldsmobile was released in multiple body styles. For example, the Ninety-Eight lineup included a luxury sedan, a Holiday sedan, a Holiday coupe, a Town sedan, and a convertible, while the Cutlass was offered in Supreme, Holiday Coupe, convertible, Sports Coupe, and Celebrity Sedan versions.
On the other hand, the Starfire received the second most powerful engine in the lineup. It was fitted with a 425ci engine rated at 375 horsepower, which used a Quadrajet carburetor and premium fuel. It was standard on the Starfire and optional on all Ninety-Eight and Delta 88 models.
The top engine this year was the Toronado Rocket, which sported a similar displacement but with a maximum output of 385 horsepower. This was standard on the Toronado.
The rest of the engines developed less power than the Starfire unit, and Oldsmobile continued to offer a six specifically for buyers interested in efficiency. The Action-Line 6 sported a displacement of 250 cubic inches and developed 155 horsepower, running on regular fuel and being offered only to F-85 buyers.
Photo: eBay seller 383-runner Oldsmobile praised the Starfire - not on every occasion, as the company had other cars to brag about, such as the Toronado - but quite often. The Starfire was fitted with thin-shell bucket seats and a floor-mounted console, and Oldsmobile wanted potential buyers to know about all of these.
“This year Starfire sports a dashing new look all its own. And style is only a starter where this performer is concerned,’ the carmaker said when taking the wraps off the new Starfire.
Sure, a Starfire isn’t the most desirable collectible, but a specimen that checks all the right boxes can’t be ignored. And this restoration candidate appears to do this, with the seller revealing that the vehicle still wears the original paint.
Photo: eBay seller 383-runner This is big, as the Starfire is likely unrestored, so whoever refreshes this car will be the first one to return it to its day-one glory. It goes without saying that this Oldsmobile deserves a restoration to factory specifications, and altering it wouldn’t make any sense, especially considering it still has the original engine under the hood.
It’s still fitted with a 425 and an automatic transmission, though you’re not getting quite the best news when opening the hood. The engine no longer starts, but if you want to see the glass half-full, you should know that it still turns over. There’s life left in this engine, and it’s up to your mechanic to give it a boost and bring the 425 back to a running shape.
The car also sports the original interior. “Basically, it’s untouched,” the seller explains.
On the other hand, we’re not getting any information about the condition of the metal. Nearly five decades in storage equals enough time for the rust invasion to do its thing.
The photos revealing the underside suggest typical rust, but my recommendation is that you raise it on a lift to figure out what is happening there. The trunk exhibits only surface problems, so there’s a chance that the vehicle wasn’t forced to deal with high humidity levels in that barn where it’s been sitting for so long.
Photo: eBay seller 383-runner Eventually, the price is the one that makes a huge difference, and in the case of a Starfire, this happens for two reasons. First, this is a project that will burn more dollars once the restoration begins, and second, a Starfire isn’t exactly the most sought-after classic.
This means it must be priced correctly to find a new home. The seller believes at least $6,000 is a fair price for this Oldsmobile, but they obviously expect to get more dollars on the car as part of this no-reserve auction. With 3 days remaining until the auction ends, the vehicle is still at zero bids, so it might be quite a challenge for this Olds to leave for a new garage on this attempt.
But as with every no-reserve auction, potential buyers might be waiting until the last few minutes to submit their offers to avoid a fierce battle. Whoever gets their hands on this car will have to pick it up from Kansas City.

U.S. Sailors, assigned to Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Thomas Hudner (DDG 116), and U.S. Coast Guard tactical team members conduct small boat operations while underway in the Caribbean Sea, Jan. 24, 2026. (U.S. Navy)
WASHINGTON — Applied Intuition has won a $2 5 million contract from the US Navy to begin deploying AI-powered sensor fusion on warships, starting with five Arl eigh Burke-class destroyers but potentially expanding “across the fleet,” the company announced this morning.
The new Intelligent Perception System (IPS) will do two jobs at once, Applied said in its announcement and a blog post . In near real time, IPS will pull in data from various cameras and infrared sensors — many of which were never designed to work together — and synthesize a single, coherent picture for the sailors. It’ll even offer helpful features like “automated alerts” when another vessel is approaching on a collision course.
Sailors aboard the USS Fitzgerald and McCain definitely could have benefited from such a capability during their back-to-back collision incidents in 2017, which killed 17 sailors and severely damaged both ships.
Meanwhile, IPS will also record the sensor data and — when bandwidth is available and security conditions permit — transmit it back to shore. There, the system’s land-based component can analyze the collected data and use it to train improved AI models for both manned and unmanned vessels.
The system even allows ships to receive updates over the air while still at sea, instead of waiting for maintenance and modernization in port, the company said. That could enable multiple refresh cycles in a single deployment.
That kind of fast-paced adaptation is reminiscent of the drone war in Ukraine and fits with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s push for rapid upgrades . It also jibes with the Pentagon’s desire to piggyback off advances in commercial tech rather than waiting for bespoke military developme nts.
Applied originally focused on self-driving cars — still a major part of its business — before it branched out into defense . At its core, the technology it’s bringing to the Navy draws on that dual-use foundation.
“The amount of data the Navy collects, and the operating environments it is constantly engaged in, [are] very similar to what we do gathering data to develop driverless cars,” Jason Brown, general manager at Applied Intuition, said in a statement to Breaking Defense.
While details obviously vary, the essentials are the same for “any autonomous system that needs to perceive environments in order to feed planning and control algorithms,” he argued. “We built those data engines for our commercial business and applied the same technical approach to naval operations.”
This new contract isn’t the first time Applied has brought its technology to the Navy. IPS builds on an earlier pilot program called DECK — short for Data Edge Collection Kit— that was tested on at least one Navy vessel earlier this year .
“DECK was massively successful,” Brown declared. “It collected data, transported it — all with commercial technology — and did it securely and within Navy operational constraints.”

Commodity Discovery Fund founder Willem Middelkoop chats with The Miner's Western Editor, Henry Lazenby, late last month in Colorado Springs.
Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 22, 2026
Commodity Discovery Fund founder Willem Middelkoop is targeting new discoveries and mines nearing production to capture gains from a commodities rally he says could last for decades.
The Netherlands-based fund, with about $316 million (€200 million) in assets under management, invests in roughly 40 to 50 discoveries across different metals, Middelkoop said. He expects persistent supply shortages to start hitting the wider economy around 2030, while major producers are only beginning to increase their exposure to early exploration.
“Everybody thinks he will be a genius because even the lousy stocks will go up,” Middelkoop told The Northern Miner Western Editor Henry Lazenby late last month in Colorado Springs. His fund focuses on two stages of the mining cycle, or the so-called Lassonde Curve: the initial discovery, when drilling can sharply increase a company’s value, and the approach to production, when investors begin pricing in future cash flow.
The timing matters because mining shares can stagnate for years after the initial excitement of a discovery fades, even in a rising metals market, he said. His approach is to take profits after the discovery rally and seek another opportunity as construction nears completion, when investors begin valuing a company’s ability to produce metal and generate cash.

His approach is to take profits after the discovery rally and seek another opportunity as construction nears completion, when investors begin valuing a company’s ability to produce metal and generate cash.

U.S. trailer orders surged in September to their highest level in nearly four years, while FTR Transportation Intelligence and ACT Research reported conflicting trends in North American Class 8 truck orders.
The mixed signals come as fleets navigate regulatory uncertainty , rising equipment costs and shifting investment priorities ahead of the 2027 model year.
U.S. trailer net orders reached 43,059 units in September, up 78% from August and 385% year over year, FTR reported. The total was the highest since December 2022 and marked an unusually strong start to the 2027 trailer ordering season.
Meanwhile, North American Class 8 truck orders totaled 19,172 units in September, down 7% from a year earlier and 15% month over month on a seasonally adjusted basis, according to ACT Research.
The contrasting results highlight a divergence in commercial vehicle demand as carriers prioritize trailer replacements while delaying some heavy-duty truck purchases amid uncertainty over federal emissions regulations and future equipment costs.
Trailer orders jump as fleets prepare for 2027
FTR said September’s trailer orders reflected substantial pent-up replacement demand following an extended period of weak equipment purchasing.
The research firm said earlier openings of 2027 trailer order books and expectations of additional tariff-related price increases may be prompting carriers to accelerate equipment purchases.
September 2026 equipment orders at a glance

U.S. trailers — ACT | 42,700 | +311%
FTR also suggested that the conclusion of the Class 8 truck pre-buy cycle and uncertainty surrounding the Environmental Protection Agency’s 2027 nitrogen oxide emissions requirements could be shifting some near-term fleet spending from trucks toward trailers.
Dan Moyer, senior analyst for commercial vehicles at FTR, said industry feedback indicates fleets are becoming more active in equipment planning.
“Rising quote activity and more requests for proposals indicate that fleets are becoming increasingly active in equipment planning,” Moyer said in a statement.
Class 8 truck orders show mixed signals
While U.S. trailer orders surged in September, research firms reported conflicting trends in North American Class 8 truck demand.
FTR Transportation Intelligence reported preliminary September Class 8 net orders of 21,300 units, up 18% from August and 3% year over year. However, ACT Research reported final September orders of 19,172 units, down 7% from a year earlier and 15% month over month on a seasonally adjusted basis.
Despite the differing estimates, both firms pointed to uncertainty surrounding the Environmental Protection Agency’s 2027 emissions regulations and truck pricing as factors influencing fleet purchasing decisions.

Medium-duty truck orders remain resilient
Demand for medium-duty commercial vehicles remained stronger than the Class 8 segment in September.
ACT reported North American Classes 5-7 truck orders of 20,297 units, up 27% year over year.
The research firm said medium-duty demand may be benefiting from dealer inventory stocking ahead of anticipated regulatory changes and higher equipment prices in 2027.
The growth in medium-duty orders contrasts with the weakness in Class 8 purchases, underscoring differences in purchasing patterns across commercial vehicle segments.

Ford Rolls Out 2027 Mustang Mach-E Trail Package
19 photos
Photo: Ford
Trail and Mustang in the same model name seems nonsensical, but the same could be said about the Rally version of the Mach-E. For model year 2027, the Ford Motor Company has borrowed a few bits from the Rally grade for the all-new Trail package. Said option adds $2,295 to the final price of the Select eAWD.
Beyond this change, Ford has opened the order banks for the 2027 Mustang Mach-E line. Across the board, the extended-range battery is now standard. This, in turn, pushes the entry price to $39,995 as opposed to $37,795 for the 2026 model.
Having cleared that up, what's in the package? Specially tuned passive struts and springs open the list, with said components lifting the front and rear axles 10 and 15 millimeters compared to the Select and Premium grades. That would be 0.4 and 0.6 inches in American English, which is not quite sufficient for the Mustang Mach-E Select eAWD Trail to be considered a true all-road machine.
Its 19-inch High Gloss Dark Carbonized Gray as-cast graphics wheels and Michelin CrossClimate 2 rubber are shared with the Mustang Mach-E Rally, ensuring proper control and grip across a wide variety of surfaces and conditions. Also shared with the Rally is the steering rack.
The Carbon Black lower fascia and Trail logo on the center armrest bring the point home. As for the reason why the Ford Motor Company decided to develop this package, bear in mind the Rally is a lot pricier. With the Trail, the Dearborn-based automaker hopes to attract customers that would have otherwise looked elsewhere due to the Rally's exorbitant starting price.
Photo: Ford Trail goodies further include standard 400-watt Pro Power Onboard, which is kind of curious because it's an optional extra on the Premium, GT, and Rally. When it comes to Trail options, Ford calls attention to a couple of things. First and foremost, the Interior Protection Package brings a cargo area protector and all-weather floor mats.
The Clamp On Cross Bar Kit by Thule is the niche option, carrying gear boxes, bicycles, and kayaks on top of the vehicle. That being said, most versions of the 2027 Mustang Mach-E for the US market ship with an 88-kWh battery. The GT and Rally level up to 91 kilowatt-hours.
$2,200 more expensive than before for its least exciting of specifications, the Mustang Mach-E drops the old secondary drive unit for a new design. While this front-mounted electric motor may deliver the same performance, Ford claims it does so at a lower cost. BlueCruise 1.5 is an extra on lesser grades, while GT and Rally get the suite by default.
Regardless of grade, BlueCruise 1.5 comes with one year plus 90 days of service included. Both the Connectivity and Security packages go standard, with a year of service included. Shadow Black and Desert Sand are the only no-extra-cost paint colors, while extra-cost options include Velocity Blue Metallic, Race Red, Star White Metallic Tri-coat, Eruption Green Metallic , Adriatic Blue Metallic, and Glacier Gray Metallic.
FoMoCo expects Trail shipments to kick off in the first quarter of 2027. Unfortunately, EPA driving range estimates will be announced later.

Elon Musk now says Tesla will start delivering Optimus humanoid robots to outside customers around the end of 2027. On Tesla’s Q3 2026 earnings call, he said the hands, the robot’s durability and its AI all still need work before then.
Those are the same three problems every humanoid robot company is fighting. And despite Musk’s claim that nobody is close to Tesla, XPeng and Hyundai’s Boston Dynamics look at least as far along.
What Tesla said about Optimus
Musk said Tesla has started early production of Optimus on its high-volume line in Fremont, where Model S and Model X used to be built. Most of a line designed for a million robots a year is installed, but he said it will take at least a year, possibly longer, to reach that rate of about 20,000 units a week, because parts of the design are still changing.
He listed what has to be solved first: the AI, the electromechanical design, and reliability, including making sure the robot doesn’t wear out after a month of use. He expects those issues to be solved around the end of next year. That’s when Tesla expects to deliver Optimus to companies outside Tesla, starting with industrial jobs that are dangerous, repetitive or need to run around the clock.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
When an analyst asked where the design was still changing, a Tesla Optimus engineer pointed to the hand as one of the hardest hardware areas, along with custom gears that still carry reliability concerns. Musk agreed the hand is the main issue, explaining that fingers need to be soft enough to handle delicate objects while surviving constant wear, and robots can’t heal like human skin can.
On the AI side, Musk said Tesla is still working through problems with the AI architecture. Tesla doesn’t have a fleet of robots collecting data the way its cars do for FSD, so it plans to build 10,000 to 20,000 robots and have them practice tasks in what it calls an Optimus Academy. Tesla also plans to put its AI5 chip in Optimus around April 2027.
Musk also promised an Optimus video within a month or two showing the robot doing tasks that aren’t pre-programmed. He argued that many humanoid demos look impressive but only run scripted routines that wouldn’t hold up in the real world.
The same problems we reported last month
None of this is new. Last month, we reported that Tesla had ramped Optimus to hundreds of units a week , but that the robots couldn’t generalize to new tasks. According to The Information, the hand and forearm had over 100 small parts assembled by hand, touch sensors had reliability issues, and the AI could take days to learn basic tasks.
Tesla’s own Q3 shareholder letter now calls the bots coming off the Fremont line “the first production-quality bots that we have manufactured.” So every Optimus before this quarter wasn’t production quality.
And the timeline keeps moving. In 2024, Musk said Tesla would build Optimus for internal use in 2025 and hopefully in high volume for other companies in 2026. In January 2025, he said Tesla would build about 10,000 robots that year, with “several thousand” doing useful work by year-end. He later admitted none were. Now external deliveries are a late-2027 target.
Is anyone ahead of Tesla?
Musk said on the call that, to the best of his knowledge, “there is no one that is even close to Tesla” on a general-purpose humanoid robot. That’s hard to square with what competitors have shown.
XPeng turned on an automated IRON production line in Guangzhou in September , with more than 80% of core processes automated. IRON has 21 degrees of freedom in each hand and runs XPeng’s physical AI model on three in-house Turing chips. XPeng plans mass production by the end of 2026, deliveries in the first half of 2027 starting with stores and malls, and a European rollout in the second half of 2027. That’s a similar timeline to Tesla’s, if not slightly ahead.
XPeng is dealing with the same reality. It hasn’t shipped IRON to a paying customer, and its timelines have slipped like everyone else’s.
Boston Dynamics started producing its electric Atlas in January and says all of its 2026 Atlas deployments are already committed, including to Google DeepMind, whose AI models Boston Dynamics is integrating. In September, it opened a robot training center at Hyundai’s Metaplant in Georgia, where Atlas is learning to sequence car parts for the assembly line. Hyundai plans to deploy 25,000 robots across its plants over the next few years. Boston Dynamics also hired Milan Kovac, Tesla’s former head of Optimus , in January.
Boston Dynamics also seems to have taken a more pragmatic approach to hands, prioritizing sturdy grippers for industrial parts over human-like dexterity. That’s less impressive in a demo, but it’s a way around the problem Tesla says is holding it back.

Himiway Took a Crack at Building an SUV E-Bike and Succeeded for Just $2,000 – Real Riders Approve
9 photos
Photo: Himiway Electric Bike
Lately, there’s been a new wave of e-bikes hitting the scene: SUVs. These are do-it-all e-bikes that can be used to carry groceries and doing so while on a trail, a beach, backwoods and more. However, they’re often priced well into the thousands and outside of the average Joe’s reach. Himiway is changing all that with their D5 2.0 20-inch, a fat-tire ride with some very neat tricks up its sleeve, especially considering its price.
Ladies and gents, since Himiway launched their 20-inch D5 2.0, nearly three million viewers have logged in to watch the clip that accompanied this ride, and frankly, I can’t blame them; Himiway really did a number here. Grab a helmet and let’s see what makes this one so special .
Photo: Himiway Electric Bike As mentioned, what we’re looking at here can be considered an SUV, even though Himiway doesn’t explicitly use the term to describe the D5. Some traits that accompany SUV e-bikes include a full-suspension frame with a step-through design, the ability to carry a diverse range of cargo, even other passengers, and a laidback geometry that can keep you in the saddle for as long as possible.
All that is in the spirit of creating a bicycle that you can use for tarmac, dirt roads, and even light trails, and as I mentioned, capable of doing all that while carrying home the literal eggs and bacon. Looking closely at the D5, that’s precisely what we have here.
At the front, we can see a suspension fork with 90 mm of travel and lockout, the latter of which helps us drive as much power to the rear wheel as possible. The rear, on the other hand, grants 100 mm of wheel travel.
Those two sources cradle a low-step frame which isn’t just for comfort and the ability to mount the bike while carrying cargo but also pushes the center of gravity as low to the ground as possible. This helps you stay stable , even when taking turns with gear on the back, middle, or the front of the D5.
Photo: Himiway Electric Bike As for the sort of cargo options we have with this one, Himiway really did a number on the D5. We can add a rack at the front of the headtube, in the middle, signaled by the mounts on the top side of the down tube, and at the rear, the latter of which has a few options available, including ones for passengers too.
According to the spec sheet, a total of 440 lbs (200 kg) is what we can work with, 80 lbs (36 kg) of which is the bike itself. Sure, it’s a heavy one, but that means stability. The 20-inch wheels and tires, the latter of which have a 4-inch cross-section, also add to the improved stability of this e-bike, a trait that countless real riders have loved.
The fat tires can also act as another source of softness, helping reduce some of the vibrations the roads throw at us. They’re also great for taming countless terrains, including sand and snow. The latter will require that you tamper with tire pressure to create a larger contact patch.
Photo: Himiway Electric Bike Now, to get all that moving, Himiway has chosen to equip the D5 with a 750 W (nominal with 1,300 W peak) motor strapped to the rear hub. This little powerhouse can also kick out a peak of up to 90 Nm (66 lb-ft), so plenty of spunk to move you and all your cargo. Depending on where you are in the world, we can see top speeds of as much as 28 mph (45 kph).
Since the D5 also includes a thumb throttle, it will classify as a Class 3 e-bike, and what I liked about Himiway here is that they give us an idea of the range we can expect under this function. Forty miles (64 km) is the peak here but under pedal assist that number jumps to 70 miles (113 km). Plenty of range.
Sure, terrain and load will have a great impact on range, but even if we can achieve 50-60 miles with pedal assist, I'd be happy. The whole framework is built upon a 48 V ecosystem and includes 15 Ah of juice. Himiway also protects the battery with an IPX6 rating, and the whole bike is rated IPX5.
Himiway also gives us the option to call upon another battery pack, more than doubling our range as the second pack is a 20 Ah one.
Photo: Himiway Electric Bike What I also need to mention is that there are both a torque and cadence sensor in place on the bike, and we can choose which kind we use as we ride around, all at the touch of a button.
Toss on a set of hydraulic disc brakes, Shimano drivetrain (11-34T) to offer some range up hills, lighting at the front and rear, and an adjustable stem, and we’re set with what looks pretty good from where I'm standing. Let’s not forget the 3.5-inch full color display with Bluetooth and control over just about any parameter an e-bike is ruled by.
Keep in mind that Himiway also build another variation of the D5 2.0 , one that’s built on 26-inch rims and 4-inch cross-section tires too.
From here, there are two ways you can go about things to see if this one is for you, and the first is to find one for sale at a distributor in your area or just take into consideration the rider reviews left on Himiway’s website as good faith that this one’s made the right way. Ride safe out there; wear a helmet.

Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 22, 2026
Bunker Hill Mining (TSX: BNKR; US-OTC: BHLL) aims to expand processing capacity at its restarted Idaho mine by nearly 40% in the second half of next year, executive chairman Richard Williams said.
The silver-lead-zinc operation near Kellogg is targeting commercial production by year-end. Williams wants to increase daily throughput to about 2,270 tonnes from the plant’s current design capacity of roughly 1,630 tonnes, subject to engineering work, a second underground haulage entrance and plant upgrades.
“Everything goes in through one portal, the Russell portal, everything comes out through the Russell portal,” Williams told The Northern Miner late last month at the Mining Forum Americas in Colorado Springs. “We can mine at 2,500 tons a day, but move that ore and feed the plant at 2,500 tons a day.”
The expansion would help underpin a strategy to use mine cash flow to fund exploration across a broader U.S. portfolio through the company’s proposed Silver47 merger . But Bunker Hill must first demonstrate reliable operations and reduce its financing costs. Williams said the company is seeking to restructure or replace an expensive silver-linked loan to free more cash for growth.

United Parcel Service has completed the conversion of four more conventional package sortation centers into automated facilities just in time for the busy holiday shipping season.
New or enhanced automated facilities are now operating in Denver, St. Paul, Minnesota; Syracuse, New York; and Portland, Oregon, UPS ( NYSE: UPS ) said this month in a news release highlighting how it has prepared for peak season.
Automation projects are part of a multiyear initiative to re-architect how parcels move through UPS’s distribution system in an effort to lower structural costs and restore margins. The strategy is to improve efficiency and focus on higher-yield segments over lightweight B2C shipments from large retailers as parcel volume growth slows from pandemic-era highs.
The network transformation involves closing 200 manual sort facilities over five years and consolidating activity into larger, modern facilities able to handle more shipments from larger catchment zones. The downsizing also has led to the elimination of 30,000 positions.
Warehouses outfitted with smart package technologies – autonomous guided vehicles, automated sort systems and systems that prioritize processing for specific customer requirements without manual intervention – improve sorting speed, package flow, accuracy and capacity. The automated systems reduce manual touches and help simplify the movement of packages through the facility, according to management.
The company is targeting about $3 billion in annual cost savings by 2028 from the restructuring.
As of July 1, 68.5% of U.S. volume flowed through an automated facility compared to 64% the year prior. The cost per piece in an automated handling facility is about 28% lower than a conventional facility with mechanical systems, which spreads out unit costs and drives operating leverage, executives said during a presentation on the company’s second-quarter results.
The facilities in Denver, St. Paul and Syracuse continued to operate while modernization upgrades were completed in phases, UPS spokeswoman Karen Tomaszewski Hill explained in an email. UPS temporarily closed the Portland facility on Swan Island and shifted operations to other locations during construction.
UPS also announced it is hiring 100,000 seasonal employees nationwide, as it does each year to ensure smooth operations during peak season. Amazon, by comparison, this week said it is hiring over 300,000 people for seasonal, part-time, and full-time roles across its U.S. core logistics network nationwide this holiday season. Amazon is now the largest parcel delivery company in the United States.
The parcel freight giant said it expects to deliver more than four billion RFID-enabled packages by the end of 2026 after completing the installation of sensors in all package delivery vehicles in the spring. The technology was previously rolled out to U.S. delivery stations and UPS Stores. RFID labels are on every package shipped from The UPS Store.
Radio frequency identification is a tracking technology suited for closed-loop environments, like an integrated package network controlled by a single company. RFID tags are cheap, but the infrastructure to read the signals is expensive. UPS previously reported it has invested more than $100 million so far to deploy RFID.
UPS is working with many customers to add RFID printers at their facilities and in the process of adding RFID readers at regional hubs. It also plans to equip aircraft with the devices.

Volkswagen’s upcoming electric car will be smaller and lower-priced than the ID. Polo, starting at around €20,000 ($22,500).
Volkswagen’s €20,000 entry-level EV will launch in 2027
The new Electric Urban Car Family is the Volkswagen Group’s answer to Chinese automakers like BYD: a new lineup of compact, entry-level electric cars.
The lineup currently includes the Volkswagen ID. Polo, ID. Cross, plus the Cupra Raval and Skoda Epiq, all based on the same MEB+ platform.
After launching the lower-priced base versions of the ID. Polo and ID. Cross, starting at €24,995 and €27,995, respectively, Volkswagen is preparing to introduce an even smaller, more affordable EV in 2027.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Volkswagen revealed the ID. EVERY1 concept car last March, a preview of its upcoming entry-level EV that will arrive in 2027 starting at around €20,000.
The ID. EVERY1, which is expected to go on sale as the ID. Up! next year, is “the last piece of the puzzle,” VW brand CEO Thomas Schäfer said, as it aims to offer the widest selection in the volume segment.
VW Brand CEO Thomas Schäfer introduces the ID. EVERY1 concept car (Source: Volkswagen)
With a length of 3,880 mm, the entry-level EV is positioned between the former Up! (3,600 mm) and ID. Polo (4,053 mm). Although that is tiny, VW said it will offer space for four passengers and a luggage compartment volume of 305 liters.
Volkswagen has yet to reveal details, but the €20,000 EV is expected to use the same 37 kWh LFP battery as the base ID. Polo and ID. Cross to keep costs down.
The ID. Polo with the 37 kWh battery has a WLTP range of up to 334 km (207 miles), so the smaller model will likely offer around the same or slightly more range.
Volkswagen ID. EVERY1 concept car (Source: Volkswagen)
Volkswagen said it will offer at least 250 km (155 miles) of range. It will also use a new 70 kW (94 hp) electric motor, enabling a top speed of 130 km/h (80 mph).
The production version of the ID. EVERY1 will be one of nine new models VW plans to launch by 2027.
Volkswagen delivered on its promise to launch the ID. Polo with the 37 kWh battery for under €25,000. Will it do the same with the new entry-level model at around €20,000? We will find out shortly.
According to Spanish auto magazine Autofácil , Volkswagen could manufacture the €20,000 EV in Spain, although Volkswagen has yet to confirm a production site.
The Group currently produces the ID. Polo and Cupra Raval at its Martorell plant, while the ID. Cross and Skoda Epiq are manufactured at the Navarra plant, both in Spain.
Volkswagen’s new Electric Urban Car Family is off to a promising start, securing nearly 150,000 orders after series production began in June.
While those in the US will miss out on the new entry-level EV, Volkswagen is launching the ID. Tiguan in 2027 as a replacement for the ID.4.

Cadillac Kicks Off 125th Anniversary With $239,000 Serialized Escalade-V Special Edition
29 photos
Photo: Cadillac / edited
Revealed ahead of the 2026 United States Grand Prix in Austin, Texas, the Escalade-V 125th Anniversary Collector Series is a very special brute. Capped at 252 units, every single example of this fellow is offered with pickable serial and vehicle identification numbers. Quite a cool personalization layer, and better still, it's stacked onto a performance SUV that is already exceptional in many regards.
Vehicles are to be labeled 1902 - 2027, and the production run will be split across two paint options. Cadillac bills the Escalade-V 125th Anniversary Collector Series as the opening act of its 125th anniversary celebrations, and furthermore, this model also marks the first Escalade to join the Collector Series .
As noted earlier, two finishes carry this program: Vibrant White Tricoat and Midnight Stone Frost. Both are exclusive to the special edition, with each taking 126 units, namely one per year from 1902 through 2027. A collector who chases a specific hue competes inside a pool of one, and the anniversary moolah buys a lot more than said experience. Visible carbon fiber is on the menu, featured on the mirror caps, engine cover, grille surround, and the lower rear fascia.
Forged 24-inch wheels add to the visual drama, framing blue-painted brake calipers. Dark-finish badging and heritage V8 puddle lamps make the 125th anniversary edition all that more desirable. Hopping inside, Cadillac went for a Black and Sheer Gray setup with eye-popping Santorini Blue stitching.
Photo: Cadillac Taking inspiration from the blue shade of the Mondrian pattern within the V-Series emblem, Santorini Blue is also used for the seat belts. A different shade of blue is used for the exclusive key fob, whereas the premium floor mats are said to have been created specifically for the Collector Series. Oddly for a V-Series model, the announcement for this one carries no maximum output figures.
Cadillac's media release does not touch on the supercharged V8 small block at all, though we do know the LT4 makes 682 horsepower and 653 pound-feet (885 Newton-meters) at full chatter in the Escalade-V. It's even punchier in the CT5-V Blackwing F1 Collector Series , in which the 6.2-liter unit develops 685 hp and 673 lb-ft (912 Nm) with the right fuel in optimal conditions.
Being an Escalade-V, the 125th Anniversary Collector Series isn't four-wheel drive. Instead, the Cadillac division of General Motors decided on all-wheel drive for this application. The full-time AWD system is the better pick than electronic 4WD for such a powerful road-oriented SUV because its active single-speed transfer case is tuned specifically for pavement-only performance, which also includes maximum launch traction.
Photo: Cadillac By comparison, the two-speed transfer case with low-range gearing is the better pick for towing and off-roading shenanigans. The Escalade-V further rocks an electronic rear limited-slip differential, actively shifting torque between the rear wheels to maximize cornering grip. The AWD system defaults to a fixed 50:50 split under normal conditions, yet the electronic brain can shift up to 67 percent to the rear wheels when pushing the vehicle hard.
Unique illuminated sill plates also mark Cadillac's birthday, and part of the $239,000 retail price can be traced back to said plates. The advertised price includes destination but excludes tax, title, and dealer fees. Given how rare this V8-powered brawler is, dealer ADMs may be truly insane.
Ordering for the first Collector Series Escalade is now open in both the US and Canada, the only markets getting this model. Global Caddy vice prez Kristian Aquilina frames the Escalade-V 125th Anniversary Collector Series as a celebration of Cadillac's heritage and the marque's approach to performance luxury, honoring the past while pointing at whatever comes next.

The Bentley Torcal's Launch Spec Bundles Naim 28-Speaker Audio, Unique Wheels, Carbon Goodies
14 photos
Photo: Bentley
Bentley waited a month after its Torcal electric vehicle's London debut to show off the launch edition. Appropriately called First Edition, this zero-emission luxobarge pairs the most powerful drivetrain with optional equipment such as Mulliner calipers, powered doors, a stupendously nice Naim audio system, and carbon-fiber stylistic touches.
Starting with the dual-motor powertrain, the limited-run Torcal First Edition makes 888 ps ( 876 hp ) and 1,350 Nm (996 lb-ft) of torque. Bentley claims 2.8 seconds to 60 mph (97 kph), while its maximum speed is estimated at 162 mph (260 kph) on summer-only performance rubber.
Truth be told, it's only natural that Bentley chose the high-output version of the Torcal for this edition. As of this writing, the most powerful Torcal yet also doubles as the brand's punchiest road-going model. Crewe wants the first wave of customer orders locked while the debut still has some heat in it, and the First Edition hands those buyers an enticing cocktail of performance and luxury.
From a visual standpoint, First Edition specifics include 22-inch wheels that mix black and Liquid Silver. Self-leveling caps are on the menu, so the winged Bs remain upright while the wheels spin. The unique wheel design is complemented by Graphene Grey brake calipers by Mulliner, namely the in-house personalization arm of the British marque.
Carbon fiber gives a number of parts a sporting look, those parts being the mirror caps, rear aerodynamic diffuser, front bumper winglets, and side sills. While on the subject of exterior goodies, First Edition badging serves as the cherry on top.
Photo: Bentley Opening the door, you're presented with First Edition treadplates that light up, bespoke seat quilting that runs contrasting chevrons, the Frosted Diamond Switchable Sunroof, and 1,780 watts of Naim audio excellence. The 28-speaker configuration includes front headrest speakers and kinaesthetic seat transducers.
What Bentley calls the Colour Specification widens the interior palette with two color splits by Mulliner, the option of a third interior color, and eight accent colors. Gloss Carbon Fibre trim pieces are standard, while alternative finishes come at no additional cost. Of course, deep-pile overmats offer the underfoot plush.
Speaking of plushness, Wellness front seats and the Rear Comfort Seat Specification are the norm here. The rear-seat treatment and the power rear doors indicate a chauffeur-oriented setup, but remember that Bentley never shied from acknowledging that its production models are engaging to drive as well.
Bentley won't say what the launch spec retails for, how many are in the offing, or when first deliveries are due in the automaker's most important of markets. On the other hand, we do know that its 113-kWh battery is good for up to 600 kilometers (375 miles) of WLTP driving range.
Similar under the skin to the Porsche Cayenne Electric, the Torcal is running an 800-volt electrical architecture that supports 400-kW charging. In optimal conditions, DC fast charging from 10 to 80 percent takes less than 20 minutes.

New Jersey lawmakers are already looking to walk back one of the country’s most controversial e-bike laws, just months after the sweeping new regulations took effect and sparked widespread backlash from riders, bicycle shops, and advocacy groups.
A newly introduced bill, S4830 , sponsored by State Senator Raj Mukherji, would remove licensing, registration, and insurance requirements for low-speed electric bicycles with motors rated at 750W or less and a maximum motor-powered speed of 20 mph (32 km/h). This includes Class 1 and Class 2 electric bicycles.
The proposal would essentially restore bicycle-like treatment for these two classes of e-bikes, importantly including throttle-equipped models that make up the majority of e-bikes sold in the state and more broadly in the US, while maintaining stricter requirements for faster and more powerful electric bicycles.
The move comes after New Jersey’s previous governor, Phil Murphy, signed a sweeping e-bike law in January following several tragic crashes involving young riders.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
That legislation, which took full effect in July, eliminated the state’s previous three-class e-bike framework and introduced licensing and registration requirements for all electric bicycles, including ordinary low-speed commuter models. Throttle-equipped and faster e-bikes also faced insurance requirements.
The backlash was intense and immediate.
As we previously reported , New Jersey bicycle shops experienced devastating sales declines after the law took effect, with some reporting drops of 20% to 90%. Several businesses were forced to lay off employees, downsize, or even close entirely as e-bike sales and usage plummeted.
Meanwhile, riders faced confusing new requirements that made e-bikes considerably less accessible, which was particularly impactful for lower-income residents, people with disabilities, and those who rely on electric bicycles for daily transportation.
The original law was intended to improve safety, but critics argued that it largely punished responsible riders instead of addressing the growing problem of high-powered electric motorcycles masquerading as bicycles. Only responsible riders actually registered their bikes as required by law, while others were deterred from cycling, and the hooligan riders who often gave e-bikes a bad name continued to ride illegally.
After all, requiring someone riding a 20 mph (32 km/h) commuter e-bike to obtain a driver’s license and register their bicycle does little to address reckless riding on machines capable of highway speeds.
The newly proposed legislation appears to acknowledge that distinction, offering a more targeted approach that could preserve reasonable safety regulations without making ordinary e-bike ownership unnecessarily complicated.
S4830 still needs to work its way through the legislature before becoming law, but for New Jersey’s struggling e-bike industry, it’s a promising sign that lawmakers may finally be listening. It is still widely argued that requiring electric bicycles from 21-28 mph (32-45 km/h) to require a driver’s license and registration is overly burdensome, but at least the state appears to be moving back toward the right direction.

2026 Paris Motor Show • 2026 Paris Motor Show: Jeep Reveals Six-Model European Strategy for 2030, Renegade Is Set to Return
JDM 2027 Subaru WRX Teased With Heavy-Duty TY85 Manual Transmission Option
10 photos
Photo: Subaru / edited
The Subaru WRX sold in the United States never lost its six-speed manual transmission. Japan's did, save for 600 units of the WRX STI Sport♯ edition. Both the American and the Japanese models use the light-duty TY75 transmission, but come November 2026, the WRX for Japan will gain the heavy-duty TY85 as a regular-production option.
In the Land of the Rising Sun, the WRX primarily uses a continuously variable box that simulates stepped shifts. Not only is this transmission design completely inappropriate for a performance-oriented application, but CVTs don't hold a candle to well-calibrated automatic trannies and twin-clutch designs.
Thankfully for Japanese customers, the CVT nightmare will soon end. To be revealed in November 2026, the regular-production manual tranny is a TY85 revised specifically for this generation of the compact all-wheel-drive sedan. The last time Subaru used the TY85 in the WRX was the previous-gen WRX STI.
A different animal from the TY75 of the WRX STI Sport♯ edition and US-market WRX, the TY85 revival wouldn't have been possible had Subaru not discovered that a partner factory still had the relevant production line. The Japanese automaker then formed a small team with the purpose of bringing the TY85 back from the dead, and the development film highlights a one-year effort.
Chief executive officer Atsushi Osaki allowed the development team to borrow the faster decision-making rhythm we normally associate with the world of motorsports, where updates have to be made quickly and effectively. Per the development film, Subaru also came up with an engine control strategy focused on naturally aspirated-like responsiveness from a turbocharged engine.
Photo: Subaru Of course, that engine is a familiar 2.4-liter turbo four-pot boxer. Unfortunately, the company isn't willing to specify if the new calibration also comes with more power and torque. Developed with input from Super Taikyu racing drivers, the TY85-equipped manual WRX promises a different shifting experience. Instead of a cable mechanism for the TY75, this fellow uses a rod-operated shift linkage.
Hearsay suggests that Subaru engineered the revised TY85 to support 500 Newton-meters (369 pound-feet) of twist, which is more than enough in a compact. Two additional manual projects are on the menu, namely a STI Sport Type RA-derived BRZ and a five-door model previewed by the Performance-B STI concept at the 2025 Japan Mobility Show.
Just like the WRX TY85, both are said to draw on motorsport knowledge. For now, everyone is looking forward to the TY85's return. Whether this heavier-duty manual transmission also comes to the US-market WRX, that remains to be seen. And yes, the other two models haven't been confirmed for the US either.
Slotted below the BRZ in the United States of America, the WRX carries a starting price of $32,495 before destination and other taxes. The WRX S4 for the Japanese market may be pricier than the BRZ, yet 4,477,000 yen for the entry grade makes it more affordable than its American cousin. At current exchange rates, that money converts to 28,530 freedom eagles.

Record fuel prices driven by the dumb oil war in Iran are fueling a faster-than-expected switch to electric trucks in the world’s biggest freight markets – and Swedish heavy truck brand Scania is scrambling to meet demand with a new factory in China.
The Swedish truck maker is set to begin manufacturing battery-powered trucks at its new Rugao assembly plant in China as soon as it receives a license, according to Scania Chief Executive Officer Christian Levin.
In an interview given in Södertälje , Levin said he expects electric trucks to account for half of China’s market by the start of 2027. “We have had to speed up those plans,” Levin explained. “It’s always quite a complicated process in China to get licenses to do different things, but I have to say: it has moved much faster than we could have imagined.”
Chinese electric semi truck sales jumped almost 80% in the first half of 2026 compared to 2025 , and are on pace to account for over 30% of all heavy trucks sold this year – and that pace is accelerating.

Scania built the Rugao plant last year, making it the Traton Group’s first wholly-owned factory in China. The facility will serve China and other Asian markets, and can build both conventional diesel and battery-powered trucks on the same assembly lines .
“It is happening quickly and that’s incredibly fascinating,” says Levin. “ It means they have found a way to expand charging infrastructure and the power grid , which is the biggest challenge we have in many countries around the world, including Europe.”
I would respond to that by saying that China has a political system that makes the betterment of society as-a-whole a higher priority than corporate profits and creating shareholder value, but nobody asked me and this isn’t one of those blogs. The Eagle mine's leaching pad is at left centre in this photo shot from a plane in June. Credit: Blair McBride
Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 22, 2026
Private entity Boroo has agreed to acquire Victoria Gold for up to $140 million (about US$100 million), advancing plans to potentially rehabilitate and restart its Eagle gold mine more than two years after a heap-leach collapse shut the Yukon operation.
The Singapore-based buyer would pay $40 million upfront and another $100 million as permitting and commercial-production milestones are met, it said in a release Thursday. Eagle lies about 375 km north of Whitehorse, in the traditional territory of the First Nation of Na-Cho Nyäk Dun.
“Our agreement to acquire Victoria Gold and the Eagle gold mine marks a pivotal turning point for this foundational Yukon asset,” Boroo CEO Dulguun Erdenebaatar said in a statement. “Over the past year, our technical and environmental teams have spent countless hours on the ground conducting rigorous due diligence to ensure that the Eagle mine can be restarted responsibly and that the site’s environmental challenges are addressed.”
Discussions with the Na-Cho Nyäk Dun remain ongoing, the company said.
The agreement offers a route out of receivership for Victoria following the June 2024 failure , which released contaminated material beyond the mine’s containment system. Court approval is still required, and the proposed purchase leaves important questions about the division of cleanup liabilities and recovery of public funds.
Restart spending
Boroo expects to spend about $800 million between 2027 and 2029 on rehabilitation, water treatment, site stabilization and a phased restart. It anticipates spending more than $600 million over the initial mine life to support and extend operations.
Those plans, together with the purchase price, underpin its announced commitment of more than $1.5 billion into Canada. The company didn’t disclose a firm production restart date or identify financing committed specifically to Eagle.
Wholly owned subsidiary Gatsuurt Mining would become Victoria’s sole shareholder. Receiver PricewaterhouseCoopers intends to seek approval from the Ontario Superior Court of Justice in early December, targeting closing around Dec. 31.
Boroo said it would assume certain remediation obligations and provide financial security to Yukon at closing. Under the proposed court order, some existing liabilities would remain with Victoria while others would transfer to a separate company that stays in receivership. The announcement didn’t disclose the amount of security.
Boroo said it had settled terms of a framework agreement with Yukon authorities covering remediation, restart and closure, effective when the acquisition closes.
Mongolian ownership
Boroo is privately held and ultimately controlled by Mongolian investor Tulga Erdenebileg, according to its June financial statements. A May 2025 takeover filing disclosed that he owned 70% through TDB Capital Singapore and Eminent Stride, with ABC Trading holding 20% and CEO Erdenebaatar 10%.
Erdenebileg also indirectly owns 29.69% of Mongolia’s Trade and Development Bank, according to the bank’s investor disclosures.
Boroo acquired Barrick’s Lagunas Norte gold mine in Peru in 2021 and controls Steppe Gold (TSX: STGO). A February filing put its Steppe interest at 56.88%.
June accounts for Boroo and a defined group of subsidiaries reported US$498.8 million in cash, US$391.7 million in borrowings and a further US$107.2 million in bonds payable to related group companies. These accounts don’t fully consolidate all Boroo subsidiaries.
The group raised US$300 million through a 9.5% bond issue last year. Its annual outlook also outlined about US$390 million of spending in 2026–27, principally for a processing expansion at Lagunas Norte.
Cleanup legacy
An independent review attributed Eagle’s June 24, 2024 failure to static liquefaction, in which material loses strength and flows. It identified poorly draining ore, accumulated water, irrigation and slope conditions as contributing factors. About 1.8 million tonnes escaped containment.
PwC became receiver on Aug. 14, 2024, following Yukon’s application. Boroo entered exclusive acquisition talks in April this year.
Yukon has authorized loans of up to $220 million to the receiver, secured by a priority claim over other creditors. That ceiling doesn’t represent the amount ultimately spent or recovered.

Union Pacific reported a 16% increase in third-quarter profit Thursday as higher freight volumes, pricing gains and fuel surcharges lifted revenue, with intermodal traffic leading the railroad’s growth.
The Omaha-based railroad (NYSE: UNP ) earned $2.08 billion, or $3.49 per diluted share, compared with $1.79 billion, or $3.01 per share, a year earlier. Adjusted earnings of $3.53 per share exceeded the $3.47 consensus estimate compiled by Zacks Investment Research.
Operating revenue increased 15% to $7.2 billion, while freight revenue excluding fuel surcharges rose 6%. Total revenue carloads grew 6% to 2.29 million. Intermodal volume increased 11% to 956,000 containers and trailers, and intermodal revenue climbed 27% to $1.52 billion. Industrial volumes rose 6%, while bulk traffic was essentially flat.
“Union Pacific’s third quarter results demonstrate our ability to safely deliver the service we sold to our customers while efficiently handling 6% volume growth,” Chief Executive Jim Vena said in the earnings release.
Operating income increased 15% to $2.94 billion. The reported operating ratio improved slightly to 59.1% from 59.2%, although the adjusted ratio deteriorated 30 basis points to 58.8%. Higher fuel prices added 140 basis points to the ratio, the company said. Workforce productivity improved 5%, while average terminal dwell declined 2% to 19.9 hours.
Union Pacific reaffirmed its forecast for high-single-digit growth in reported earnings per share for 2026 and updated its capital spending plan to $3.5 billion. Vena also pointed to upcoming steps in the Surface Transportation Board ’s review of the railroad’s proposed merger with Norfolk Southern (NYSE: NSC ).
Why it matters: Union Pacific’s earnings show how intermodal growth and pricing gains are supporting profits even as higher fuel costs pressure operating efficiency.

A tractor-trailer carrying fresh tomatillos arrived at California’s Otay Mesa port of entry from Mexico on October 14. The commercial shipment had a delivery destination in the United States. During an inspection, U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers discovered nearly 1,600 pounds of methamphetamine mixed with the produce. Authorities estimated the narcotics’ street value at approximately $2.5 million.
Federal officials also took immigration action against the truck driver. CBP confirmed that authorities served the motorist with a visa cancellation. The agency cited Section 212(a)(2)(C)(i) of the Immigration and Nationality Act as the legal basis. That provision concerns individuals whom authorities know or have reason to believe participated in illicit drug trafficking.
The statute also covers individuals who knowingly assisted, conspired in or colluded with traffickers. Immigration authorities can apply this provision without securing a criminal conviction. However, CBP has not disclosed what evidence supported the driver’s visa cancellation. Investigators have not publicly established whether the driver knowingly participated in transporting the narcotics.
Federal agencies announce $2.5 million seizure
CBP announced the discovery on October 16 during a news conference involving multiple federal law enforcement agencies. Participants included the Office of Field Operations, Border Patrol, Air and Marine Operations, and Homeland Security Investigations. The original announcement did not disclose any action against the driver.
Earlier this month, CBP reported another major methamphetamine seizure at Texas’ Laredo World Trade Bridge. Officers discovered approximately 3,396 pounds concealed within a commercial shipment of salt. Authorities valued those drugs at $30.4 million, roughly $8,900 per pound compared with $1,560 at Otay Mesa. CBP confirmed that California’s $2.5 million estimate reflected San Diego-area street values but did not fully explain the difference.
Following the announcement, FreightWaves contacted CBP for additional information about the inspection and trucking operation. The agency declined to explain what prompted officers to examine the shipment. Investigators also withheld details about the concealment method.
Investigation leaves carrier involvement unresolved
CBP has not identified the motor carrier or established publicly whether anyone involved knew about the narcotics. Authorities also declined to confirm whether officers arrested the driver or transferred him to Homeland Security Investigations. The agency declined to provide additional information about potential criminal charges, citing the ongoing investigation.
Why it matters
Commercial drug seizures raise important questions about cargo security, carrier accountability and shipment oversight. Consistent verification procedures and documented custody help transportation professionals identify discrepancies and establish responsibility when authorities uncover illegal freight.

Industrial output help U.S. railroads steel themselves against increasing demand and show some mettle amid uncertain economic conditions.
For the week ending Oct. 17, total U.S. weekly rail traffic was 540,135 carloads and intermodal units, up 8.5% from the same week a year ago, according to the Association of American Railroads .

Nine of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025.
(Chart: AAR)
Metallic ores and metals used in steelmaking and other production led all gainers, up 14.5%. Domestic raw-steel production increased 4.1% from the previous week, the latest American Iron and Steel Institute figures show. Petroleum and related products improved 8.8%, and grain was ahead 7%.
Nonmetallic minerals such as sand and stone was the only category to retreat, down 3.2% y/y.

Register for Lytx’s Oct. 27 webinar on building a defensible safety record .
Since 1994, many courts interpreted the Federal Aviation Administration Act (FAAAA) to shield brokers from state-law negligent hiring lawsuits, finding that such claims were preempted since they related to a broker’s services in arranging transportation. In May, the Supreme Court closed that door. In Montgomery v. Caribe Transport II, LLC , the justices ruled unanimously that freight brokers can face negligent hiring and carrier-selection claims under state law, meaning a broker who knew, or reasonably should have known, that a carrier had safety problems can no longer treat the matter as someone else’s responsibility. A unanimous decision that sent a clear signal to the industry that safety is everyone’s job, not just the motor carrier’s.
The ruling does not create strict liability for brokers, and it does not change the underlying safety requirements carriers must meet. What it changes is the burden of proof. A broker’s carrier-selection process (which would include what it knew, when it knew it, and what it did in response) is now far more likely to be scrutinized after an accident. That makes the broker’s documentation of due diligence part of their legal exposure.
The scrutiny cuts both ways for carriers. A clean public record of things like current authority, active insurance, or an acceptable FMCSA safety rating may no longer be evidence that a broker did enough. Brokers now have reason to look past those baseline checks toward carriers who can demonstrate an active, ongoing safety management program such as a video telematics program that identifies and addresses risks and documents the results of changes. Two carriers can look identical on paper and still represent very different levels of risk. A documented safety program makes a carrier choice more defensible for the broker later.
That is a notable shift in emphasis. For years, a safety record was treated as a compliance checkbox. Carriers would maintain the broad strokes of compliance to stay on the road, but would rarely use safety records to actively market or to win freight. Under the standard taking shape now, a documented safety record is a necessary credential. It’s proof that a carrier can offer a broker, an insurer, or a court that it took safety seriously prior to an incident. It is a competitive advantage in broker selection of a carrier.
A few practices separate a proactive safety management program from a reactive one. Fleets that have gone through this transition tend to build in an adjustment period before formal coaching begins, so early reviews reflect real driving patterns rather than first-week unfamiliarity with a new system. They pair event review with consistent, documented coaching conversations, rather than letting footage accumulate without follow-up. They unify compliance data and safety performance data rather than managing elements such as hours-of-service records and driving-behavior data as unrelated metrics.
The ruling also lands in the context of other changes in freight risk. Insurance underwriters have been reassessing carrier risk profiles for several underwriting cycles now, and nuclear verdicts in trucking litigation have already pushed premiums higher industry-wide. Montgomery adds another layer of exposure on top of that trend, and carriers able to point to an active, documented safety program are better positioned heading into renewal conversations, not just broker conversations.
None of this requires predicting exactly how state courts will apply Montgomery over the next few years. It requires recognizing that the standard of proof has changed, and that “documented safety performance” is a higher bar than bare-minimum compliance.
Lytx ® has spent 15 years in the DOT compliance space, helping fleets manage ELD compliance, improve safety scores, and build the kind of documented safety programs that brokers, insurers, and shippers are increasingly expecting to see. The company is hosting a webinar on Oct. 27 at 10 a.m. PST aimed at carrier safety, risk, compliance, and legal leaders, focused on how to make an existing safety program demonstrable. You’ll hear what brokers are looking for, what a defensible safety record looks like in practice, and what the fleets staying ahead of this are doing differently. Registration is available here.
